title: Four Billion Tiny Insects Cross the Sea to Britain
subject: hoverfly

scenes.text: Up to four billion tiny insects cross the sea to and from Britain every year.
Radar caught them flying as high as a thousand meters. They aren't bees or butterflies.
In autumn, about a billion more fly back to the mainland than arrived in spring. That's roughly twenty-eight tons.
On the way, they pollinate many billions of flowers.
They're hoverflies, and their larvae eat up to ten trillion aphids.
So the next tiny hoverer at your flowers may have just crossed the sea.
